parts.label: (a)
parts.text: By reference to the definition of gravitational potential, explain why gravitational potential is a negative quantity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
Two stars A and B have their surfaces separated by a distance of $1.4 \times 10^{12} \text{m}$, as illustrated in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:figure_1_1}}

Fig. 1.1

Point P lies on the line joining the centres of the two stars. The distance $x$ of point P from the surface of star A may be varied.

The variation with distance $x$ of the gravitational potential $\phi$ at point P is shown in Fig. 1.2.

{{figure:figure_1_2}}

Fig. 1.2

A rock of mass $180 \text{kg}$ moves along the line joining the centres of the two stars, from star A towards star B.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Use data from Fig. 1.2 to calculate the change in kinetic energy of the rock when it moves from the point where $x = 0.1 \times 10^{12} \text{m}$ to the point where $x = 1.2 \times 10^{12} \text{m}$. State whether this change is an increase or a decrease.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
At a point where $x = 0.1 \times 10^{12} \text{m}$, the speed of the rock is $v$.

Determine the minimum speed $v$ such that the rock reaches the point where $x = 1.2 \times 10^{12} \text{m}$.
